verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要拿一把快刀，当作剃头刀，用这刀剃你的头发和你的胡须，用天平将须发平分。
verses.en: “As for you, son of man, take a sharp sword and use it as a barber’s razor.[NOTE:1] Shave off some of the hair from your head and your beard.[NOTE:2] Then take scales and divide up the hair you cut off.
notes: The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT.
Heb, “pass (it) over your head and your beard.”
verses.commentary:
5:1 "son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

▣ "take a sharp sword" The VERB (BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERATIVE)
is a command. The normal instrument for shaving was a "razor" (BDB 1074, cf. Num. 6:5; 8:7). However, here a
"sword" (BDB 352, Ezek. 5:1,2 [twice], 12 [twice], 17) is used. It was a symbol of the coming judgment
(cf. Ezek. 6:3,8, 11,12; 7:15). This same judgment is alluded to in Isa. 7:20, using the word "razor."
Shaving the hair and beard was a sign of shame (cf. 2 Sam. 10:4). The sword was a symbol of death and devastation.
Judah would reap a divine judgment for her sins (i.e. Nebuchadnezzar's army).

▣ "scales for weighing" This is a Hebrew CONSTRUCT (BDB 24 and 1054). Scales were
used in weighing the purchase of agricultural items. When used in an unfair way it became an idiom of
exploitation and unfairness (cf. Deut. 25:13-16; Prov. 11:1). In contrast, God's scales (i.e. of justice)
were fair and reliable. Judah was weighed by YHWH and found wanting! Judah deserved both

- shame (i.e. sword for shaving)

- judgment (i.e. scales for weighing)

verses.zh: 围困城的日子满了，你要将三分之一在城中用火焚烧，将三分之一在城的四围用刀砍碎，将三分之一任风吹散；我也要拔刀追赶。
verses.en: Burn a third of it in the fire inside the city when the days of your siege are completed. Take a third and slash it with a sword all around the city. Scatter a third to the wind, and I will unleash a sword behind them.
verses.commentary:
5:2-4 Ezekiel's hair (usually a sign of religious devotion, cf. Numbers 6; Judges 16-17; 2 Sam. 10:4-5)
was to be shaved, divided, and disposed of in specific ways.

- one-third burned at the center of the city (i.e. the model of Jerusalem of chapter 4) when
Jerusalem falls, Ezek. 5:2

- one-third cut with the sword all around the city (i.e. the model of Jerusalem of chapter 4), Ezek. 5:2

- one-third scattered to the wind, Ezek. 5:2 (i.e. the scattering of exiles)

- a few hairs were tied into Ezekiel's robe, Ezek. 5:3

- a few hairs put in a fire, which will spread to all Judah, Ezek. 5:4 (fire is often used in Ezekiel as a judgment of God,
cf. Ezek. 5:2,4; 10:2,6-7; 15:4-7; 16:41; 19:12,14; 20:47-48; 21:31-32; 23:25,47; 24:10,12; 30:8,14,16; 39:6

The symbolic act seems to mean that one-third of the inhabitants of Jerusalem will be killed by
the sword, one-third will be killed by famine and one-third will be scattered among the nations (cf. Ezek. 5:2).

In Ezek. 5:3 the concept of remnant appears, which occurs throughout the OT in God's dealing
with His rebellious covenant people (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:22; Isa. 6:13; 10:22; Jer. 23:3; Ezek. 5:3; 6:8-10; 11:13;
Zech. 13:8, 9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, three senses

verses.zh: 你要从其中取几根包在衣襟里，
verses.en: But take a few strands of hair[NOTE:1] from those and tie them in the ends of your garment.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “from there a few in number.” The word “strands” has been supplied in the translation for clarification.
Objects could be carried in the end of a garment (Hag 2:12).

verses.zh: 再从这几根中取些扔在火中焚烧，从里面必有火出来烧入以色列全家。
verses.en: Again, take more of them and throw them into the fire,[NOTE:1] and burn them up. From there a fire will spread to all the house of Israel.
notes: Heb “into the midst of” (so KJV, ASV). This phrase has been left untranslated for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：这就是耶路撒冷。我曾将她安置在列邦之中；列国都在她的四围。
verses.en: “This is what the Sovereign Lord says: This is Jerusalem; I placed her in the center of the nations with countries all around her.
verses.commentary:
5:5 This verse affirms the purposeful plan of God to place His people where they must depend on His care
and protection. They were not a large, powerful people (cf. Deut. 7:7), but their land was at the crossroads
of the major Near Eastern powers of Babylon, Assyria, Anatolia, and Egypt.

God wanted to use His people planted in such a prominent place to educate and draw the surrounding
peoples (i.e. "the nations) to Himself (cf. Deut. 4:6-8, see The Prophecy of Ezekiel by Feinberg, p. 37).
Because of Israel's disobedience, all they (i.e. the nations) saw was the judgment of God
(cf. Ezek. 5:7-9; 36:22-36).

▣ "at the center of the nations" When this phrase is seen in light of

- Ezek. 38:12

- the use of the imagery of "navel" in Near Eastern religion (cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 333-334)

it becomes a significant theological statement. YHWH's people were the revelatory epicenter of the
world. His eternal, universal, redemptive plan involved them. Their continuing covenant unfaithfulness was a major
barrier to revealing His faithful character, which will be expressed in the "New Covenant,"
which is not based on human performance (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 她行恶，违背我的典章，过于列国；干犯我的律例，过于四围的列邦，因为她弃掉我的典章。至于我的律例，她并没有遵行。
verses.en: Then she defied my regulations and my statutes, becoming more wicked than the nations[NOTE:1] and the countries around her.[NOTE:2] Indeed, they[NOTE:3] have rejected my regulations, and they do not follow my statutes.
notes: The nations are subject to a natural law according to Gen 9; see also Amos 1:3-2:3 and Jonah 1:2.
Heb “she defied my laws, becoming wicked more than the nations, and [she defied] my statutes [becoming wicked] more than the countries around her.”

One might conclude that the subject of the plural verbs is the nations/countries, but the context (vv. 5-6a) indicates that the people of Jerusalem are in view. The text shifts from using the feminine singular (referring to personified Jerusalem) to the plural (referring to Jerusalem’s residents). See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 1:73.
verses.commentary:
5:6-7 "statutes. . .ordinances" See Ezek. 5:6, 7 .

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：因为你们纷争过于四围的列国，也不遵行我的律例，不谨守我的典章，并以遵从四围列国的恶规尚不满意，
verses.en: “Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Because you are more arrogant[NOTE:1] than the nations around you,[NOTE:2] you have not followed my statutes and have not carried out my regulations. You have not even[NOTE:3] carried out the regulations of the nations around you!
notes: Traditionally this difficult form has been derived from a hypothetical root הָמוֹן (hamon), supposedly meaning “be in tumult/uproar,” but such a verb occurs nowhere else. It is more likely that it is to be derived from a root מָנוֹן (manon), meaning “disdain” (see L. C. Allen, Ezekiel [WBC], 1:52). A derivative from this root is used in Prov 29:21 of a rebellious servant. See HALOT 600 s.v. מָנוֹן.
You are more arrogant than the nations around you. Israel is accused of being worse than the nations in Ezek 16:27; 2 Kgs 21:11; Jer 2:11.
Some Hebrew mss and the Syriac omit the words “not even.” In this case they are being accused of following the practices of the surrounding nations. See Ezek 11:12.
verses.commentary:
5:7

NASB
"you have more turmoil"

NKJV
"your have multiplied disobedience more"

NRSV
"you are more turbulent"

TEV
"you have caused more trouble"

NJB
"your disorders are worse"

JPSOA
"you have outdone"

REB
"you have been more insubordinate"

NET
"you are more arrogant"

This NOUN form appears only here in the OT (BDB 243,
KB 632, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT). Its basic meaning may be

- to rebel

- to raze

- to be turbulent

- Some scholars assert that it comes from a different root meaning "to disdain" or "to be weak."

▣

NASB
"you have not walked. . .nor observed" (twice)

LXX, NKJV, Peshitta
"have not walked in. . .nor kept"

NRSV
"not followed. . .or kept"

TEV
"by not obeying. . .or keeping"

NJB
"you do not keep. . .or respect"

REB
"have not conformed. . .have not kept"

JPSOA
"you have not obeyed. . .or followed"

The MT has the negative (לא) twice, but the RSV leaves out the negatives. The
UBS Text Project, p. 10, gives the MT a "B" rating. The only English translation that removes the two "nots" is the RSV,
which follows some Hebrew and Syriac manauscripts.

Because of the last phrase of this verse, Ezek. 5:6, and 16:27, this phrase must mean that Judah sinned
worse than the surrounding nations! Her idolatries reached new heights!

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：看哪，我与你反对，必在列国的眼前，在你中间，施行审判；
verses.en: “Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I—even I—am against you,[NOTE:1] and I will execute judgment[NOTE:2] among you while the nations watch.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “I challenge you.” The phrase “I am against you” may be a formula for challenging someone to combat or a duel. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 1:201-2, and P. Humbert, “Die Herausforderungsformel ‘hinnenî ’êlékâ’” ZAW 45 (1933): 101-8. The Hebrew text switches to a second feminine singular form here, indicating that personified Jerusalem is addressed (see vv. 5-6a). The address to Jerusalem continues through v. 15. In vv. 16-17 the second masculine plural is used, as the people are addressed.

The Hebrew text uses wordplay here to bring out the appropriate nature of God’s judgment. “Execute” translates the same Hebrew verb translated “carried out” (literally meaning “do”) in v. 7, while “judgment” in v. 8 and “regulations” in v. 7 translate the same Hebrew noun (meaning “regulations” or in some cases “judgments” executed on those who break laws). The point seems to be this: God would “carry out judgments” against those who refused to “carry out” his “laws.”

Heb “in the sight of the nations.”sn This is one of the ironies of the passage. The Lord set Israel among the nations for honor and praise as they would be holy and obey God’s law, as told in Ezek 5:5 and Deut 26:16-19. The practice of these laws and statutes would make the peoples consider Israel wise. (See Deut 4:5-8, where the words for laws and statutes are the same as those used here). Since Israel did not obey, they are made a different kind of object lesson to the nations, not by their obedience but in their punishment, as told in Ezek 5:8 and Deut 29:24-29. Yet Deut 30 goes on to say that when they remember the cursings and blessings of the covenant and repent, God will restore them from the nations to which they have been scattered.
verses.commentary:
5:8 "I, even I" This is very emphatic! YHWH will act against Israel to maintain the truthfulness of
His own revelation. The covenant God acts against the covenant people!

God wanted to reach all nations through Israel. She was the means, not the goal!

▣ "I will execute judgment among you in the sight of the nations" It must be remembered that Israel
was called to be "a kingdom of priests" (cf. Exod. 19:5,6). She will be a testimony, either positively or
negatively (cf. Ezek. 5:15; Ezek. 36:23-36).

verses.zh: 并且因你一切可憎的事，我要在你中间行我所未曾行的，以后我也不再照着行。
verses.en: I will do to you what I have never done before and will never do again because of all your abominable practices.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “abominable idols.”
verses.commentary:
5:9 God will execute judgment against His own covenant people more severely than other judgments
because Israel knew Him, knew His will and yet violated them (cf. Luke 12:48; Rom. 9:4-5)!

verses.zh: 在你中间父亲要吃儿子，儿子要吃父亲。我必向你施行审判，我必将你所剩下的分散四方（方：原文是风）。」
verses.en: Therefore, fathers will eat their sons within you, Jerusalem,[NOTE:1] and sons will eat their fathers. I will execute judgments on you, and I will scatter any survivors[NOTE:2] to the winds.[NOTE:3]
notes: In context “you” refers to the city of Jerusalem. To make this clear for the modern reader, “Jerusalem” has been supplied in the translation in apposition to “you.”sn This cannibalism would occur as a result of starvation due to the city being besieged. It is one of the judgments threatened for a covenant law violation (Lev 26:29; see also Deut 28:53; Jer 19:9; Lam 2:20; Zech 11:9).
Heb “all of your survivors.”
Heb “to every wind.”
verses.commentary:
5:10 "the fathers will eat their sons" This is one of the horrors of siege warfare. It was foretold
in Lev. 26:29 and Deut. 28:53. The cannibalism is predicted in Jer. 19:9 and fulfilled in Lam. 2:20 and 4:10.
Flavius Josephus also tells us of the same horrendous acts occurring in the siege of Jerusalem by Titus
in A.D. 70.

▣ "scatter all your remnant to every wind" The concept of remnant was alluded to in Ezek. 5:3.

This VERB (BDB 279, KB 280, Piel PERFECT with
waw) refers literally to winnowing grain (i.e. separating the husk and grain), but it is often used as imagery of
judgment (i.e. exile, cf. Deut. 30:15-16; 31:15-16; Ezek. 20:23). God's very own people become the "husk"!

Notice it is YHWH, not the nations, who scatters His people (cf. Ezek. 5:10,12; 6:8; 12:14-15;
20:23; 22:15; 36:19). It was not the power of the gods of the nations or their military, but the righteous judgment of
YHWH that scatters His people for breaking the covenant (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28).

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

verses.zh: 主耶和华说：「我指着我的永生起誓，因你用一切可憎的物、可厌的事玷污了我的圣所，故此，我定要使你人数减少，我眼必不顾惜你，也不可怜你。
verses.en: “Therefore, as surely as I live, says the Sovereign Lord, because you defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable idols and with all your abominable practices, I will withdraw; my eye will not pity you, nor will I spare[NOTE:1] you.
notes: The meaning of the Hebrew term is primarily emotional: “to pity,” which in context implies an action, as in being moved by pity in order to spare them from the horror of their punishment.
verses.commentary:
5:11 "So as I live declares the Lord God" This is an oath used
fourteen times in Ezekiel. It is a play on the word YHWH (i.e. a form of the VERB "to be"), which means
"the only-living, ever-living God." God is true to His word (i.e. Isa. 55:9-11)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "because you have defiled My sanctuary" This is described in detail in chapter 8
(cf. Ezek. 9:7; 23:38; 43:6-9).

▣ "abominations" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION

NASB
"I will also withdraw"

NKJV
"I will also diminish you"

NRSV, TEV
"I will cut you down"

NJB, LXX
"I too shall reject you"

JPSOA
"I in turn will shear [you] away"

REB
"I in turn shall destroy you"

Peshitta
"I will scatter away"

This refers to

- Ezekiel's vision of the glory of YHWH and His Spirit leaving the temple in Jerusalem and moving east to be with the exiles (cf. chapters 8-11)

- YHWH shearing Israel (cf. Ezek. 5:1; same VERB, BDB 175, KB 203, used of "shaving" in Isa. 15:2; Jer. 48:37)

There is some question about what this VERB (BDB 175, KB 203, Qal
IMPERFECT) means. The basic meaning is to

- diminish (cf. Exod. 5:8,19; Deut. 4:2; Jer. 26:2)

- restrain (cf. Job 15:4,8; Niphal Num. 9:7)

- withdraw (cf. Job. 36:7; Niphal Num. 36:3,4)

- cut down (see NRSV, TEV, JPSOA, relating back to the shaving of Ezek. 5:1-2)

The results of YHWH abandoning His own temple is a complete rejection of the inhabitants of Jerusalem as
His people. Notice He will

- have no pity, BDB 299, KB 298, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ezek. 7:9; 8:18; 9:5,10

- not spare, BDB 328, KB 328, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ezek. 7:9; 8:18; 9:5,10

Instead of the promise of great numbers of Israelites (i.e. stars, sand, dust; see full note at Gen. 13:16), YHWH will extensively
reduce their numbers until only a remnant is left (cf. Ezek. 5:3).

▣ "My eye" This is an anthropomorphic way of referring to God's personal attention to His covenant people.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

verses.zh: 你的民三分之一必遭瘟疫而死，在你中间必因饥荒消灭；三分之一必在你四围倒在刀下；我必将三分之一分散四方（方：原文是风），并要拔刀追赶他们。
verses.en: A third of your people will die of plague or be overcome by the famine within you.[NOTE:1] A third of your people will fall by the sword surrounding you,[NOTE:2] and a third I will scatter to the winds. I will unleash a sword behind them.
notes: The judgment of plague and famine comes from the covenant curse (Lev 26:25-26). As in v. 10, the city of Jerusalem is figuratively addressed here.
Judgment by plague, famine, and sword occurs in Jer 21:9; 27:13; Ezek 6:11, 12; 7:15.

verses.zh: 「我要这样成就怒中所定的；我向他们发的忿怒止息了，自己就得着安慰。我在他们身上成就怒中所定的那时，他们就知道我―耶和华所说的是出于热心；
verses.en: Then my anger will be fully vented; I will exhaust my rage on them, and I will be appeased.[NOTE:1] Then they will know that I, the Lord, have spoken in my jealousy[NOTE:2] when I have fully vented my rage against them.
notes: Or “calm myself.”

The Hebrew noun translated “jealousy” is used in the human realm to describe suspicion of adultery (Num 5:14ff.; Prov 6:34). Since Israel’s relationship with God was often compared to a marriage, this term is appropriate here. The term occurs elsewhere in Ezekiel in 8:3, 5; 16:38, 42; 23:25.
verses.commentary:
5:13 Notice all the "My's" in this verse! They denote YHWH's personal righteous character.

- My anger (BDB 60)

- My wrath (BDB 404)

- My zeal (or "jealousy," BDB 888; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUSY, ZEAL)

- My wrath (BDB 404)

NASB, REB
"I shall be appeased"

NKJV
"I will be avenged"

NRSV
"satisfy myself"

TEV
"until I am satisfied"

NJB
"I have sated my fury"

LXX
"when I spend my anger"

JPSOA
"when I vent all My fury"

Peshitta
"I will be comforted"

The VERB (BDB 636, KB 688, Hithpael PERFECT with waw)
in this stem can have several meanings.

- "be sorry" or "have compassion," cf. Deut. 32:36 (which does not fit this context)

- "rue" or "repent," cf. Num. 23:19 (which does not fit this context)

- "comfort oneself," cf. Gen. 37:35; Ps. 119:52 (which could fit)

- "ease oneself by taking vengeance," cf. Gen. 27:42 (by planning evil); also this same connotation is
expressed in the Niphal stem (cf. Isa. 1:24). This does fit the context best!

God's anger will cease after His judgment (cf. Ezek. 16:42; 21:17; 24:13). His purpose is an obedient people,
not a settled wrath! His acts of judgment are meant to restore, not totally annihilate!

Also note that it is not the people's repentance, but YHWH's mercy that limits and concludes judgment!

▣ "in My zeal" This NOUN (BDB 888) is translated "ardor," "zeal,"
and "jealousy." Therefore, it could be understood as

- YHWH jealous for His word

- YHWH jealous for His covenant people.

Judah had violated YHWH's covenant and YHWH's love!

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUSY, ZEAL

verses.zh: 并且我必使你在四围的列国中，在经过的众人眼前，成了荒凉和羞辱。
verses.en: “I will make you desolate and an object of scorn among the nations around you, in the sight of everyone who passes by.
verses.commentary:
5:14-15 This reflects Deut. 28:37. Moses told the people of Israel that if they kept the Mosaic Covenant they would be
blessed, but if they broke it they would be cursed (cf. Lev. 26).

Notice the list of things YHWH will do to His disobedient covenant people.

- "I will make you a desolation," Ezek. 5:14 (BDB 352, a place of waste and ruin)

- "a reproach among the nations," Ezek. 5:14 (BDB 357, a shame, disgrace, scorn, cf. Ezek. 5:15)

- "a reviling," Ezek. 5:15 (BDB 154, this FEMININE NOUN form is found only here and means a
taunt or someone as the object of blasphemous words)

- "a warning," Ezek. 5:15 (BDB 416, "chastening" or "chastisement of God")

- "an object of horror," Ezek. 5:15 (BDB 1031, "appalling object," horror," cf. Deut. 28:37; Jer. 25:9,11,18,38)

Notice how God describes His coming judgments (i.e. Ezek. 5:15)

- in anger (BDB 60, cf. Ezek. 5:13)

- in wrath (BDB 404, cf. Ezek. 5:13[twice])

- in raging rebukes (BDB 407 CONSTRUCT 404, cf. Ezek. 25:17)

YHWH acts against disobedient Judah as a witness to the nations of His righteous character
(i.e. Ezek. 5:14-15; 36:22-38). It has always been YHWH's plan to reveal Himself through Israel (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6;
see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN). He wanted
it to be in blessing, but if necessary, He will witness in judgment!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HORROR, REPROACH, CURSE

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 这样，我必以怒气和忿怒，并烈怒的责备，向你施行审判。那时，你就在四围的列国中成为羞辱、讥刺、警戒、惊骇。这是我―耶和华说的。
verses.en: You will be[NOTE:1] an object of scorn and taunting,[NOTE:2] a prime example of destruction[NOTE:3] among the nations around you when I execute judgments against you in anger and raging fury.[NOTE:4] I, the Lord, have spoken!
notes: This reading is supported by the versions and by the Dead Sea Scrolls (11QEzek). Most Masoretic Hebrew mss read: “it will be,” but if the final he (ה) is read as a mater lectionis, as it can be with the second masculine singular perfect, then they are in agreement. In either case the subject refers to Jerusalem.
The Hebrew word occurs only here in the OT. A related verb means “revile, taunt” (see Ps 44:16).

Heb “discipline and devastation.” These words are omitted in the Old Greek. The first term pictures Jerusalem as a recipient or example of divine discipline; the second depicts her as a desolate ruin (see Ezek 6:14).
Heb “in anger and in fury and in rebukes of fury.” The heaping up of synonyms emphasizes the degree of God’s anger.
verses.commentary:
5:15

NASB, NKJV
"it"

NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB, JPSOA, LXX, Peshitta, Targums, Vulgate, DSS
"you"

The MT has "it shall be" (BDB 224, KB 243,
Qal PERFECT with waw, FEMININE SINGULAR), which refers to Jerusalem. Here,
the city stands for God's people, set by Him among the nations as a witness (cf. v. 5). Even the exiles were used by
YHWH to spread His name among the nations.

The UBS Text Project, p. 11, gives "you" a "C" rating.

verses.zh: 那时，我要将灭人、使人饥荒的恶箭，就是射去灭人的，射在你们身上，并要加增你们的饥荒，断绝你们所倚靠的粮食；
verses.en: I will shoot against them deadly,[NOTE:1] destructive[NOTE:2] arrows of famine,[NOTE:3] which I will shoot to destroy you.[NOTE:4] I will prolong a famine on you and will remove the bread supply.[NOTE:5]
notes: The Hebrew word carries the basic idea of “bad, displeasing, injurious” but has the nuance “deadly” when used of weapons (see Ps 144:10).
Heb “which are/were to destroy.”
The language of this verse may have been influenced by Deut 32:23.
Or “which were to destroy those whom I will send to destroy you” (cf. NASB).
Heb, “break the staff of bread.” The bread supply is compared to a staff that one uses for support. See 4:16, as well as the covenant curse in Lev 26:26.
verses.commentary:
5:16-17 These verses continue the items of destruction mentioned in Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28.
YHWH is true to His word (cf. Ezek. 5:17c).

Note the litany of judgments.

- the deadly arrows of famine, Ezek. 5:16,17; Deut. 28:20-26

- wild beasts, Ezek. 5:17 (cf. Lev. 26:22; Deut. 32:24)

- plague, Ezek. 5:17 (cf. Lev. 26:21)

- bloodshed, Ezek. 5:17

- sword, Ezek. 5:17

These were meant to turn His people back to Him in repentance and faith (cf. Deuteronomy 28; 30:1-10).

5:16 The MT, at the beginning of v. 16, has "against them," both "them" and "you," but the verse implies has "you," which
fits the context better. The UBS Text Project, p. 11, thinks "them" is original (i.e. "B" rating).

▣ "and break the staff of bread" The term "staff" (BDB 641), following its usages with Moses' staff
(i.e. God's power in the hands of Moses), may be an idiom for a divine supply. Therefore, in this context it is
parallel to famine. This phrase is used several times (cf. Lev. 26:26; Ps. 105:16; Ezek. 4:16; 5:16; 14:13).

verses.zh: 又要使饥荒和恶兽到你那里，叫你丧子，瘟疫和流血的事也必盛行在你那里；我也要使刀剑临到你。这是我―耶和华说的。」
verses.en: I will send famine and wild beasts against you, and they will take your children from you.[NOTE:1] Plague and bloodshed will overwhelm you,[NOTE:2] and I will bring a sword against you. I, the Lord, have spoken!”
notes: Heb “will bereave you.”
Heb “will pass through you.” This threat recalls the warning of Lev 26:22, 25 and Deut 32:24-25.
verses.commentary:
5:17 "they will bereave you of children" The wild beasts will kill the children of the disobedient Jerusalemites.
Notice, like David's first child with Bathsheba, the children pay the price for their parent's sin (cf. Deut. 5:9).
However, please note Deut. 5:10 and 7:9. His love reaches to "a thousand generations"! Judgment is God's strange work
(cf. Isa. 28:21; Lam. 3:33).

- Why did God send a prophet to His people whom He knew would not listen?

- What do the symbolic acts of chapters 4 and 5 represent?

- What is the major message that Ezekiel is trying to convey to the exiles in Babylon?
